To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a method for imaging the metabolism of the most common PET imaging agent (FDG) at the cellular level and that we developed an improved whole-body PET imaging approach.

1) FDG uptake is a function of the glucose transporter (GLUT) and the hexokinase activity in cells; 2) a novel, compact PET/MR system has been developed that is capable of high-resolution imaging of small animals and 3) hyperpolarization of 13C-pyruvate allows the detection of the conversion of pyruvate to lactate and to alanine in tumors in vivo.

(1) we have developed a new PET system that is capable of high resolution whole-body imaging, (2) we have demonstrated the ability to detect cancer in small animals using this system, (3) we have demonstrated that we can detect cancer in a large animal (dog) model of human cancer using this system, and (4) we have demonstrated in a large animal model of human cancer that this system can be used for longitudinal studies.

the development of new imaging agents and imaging systems that promise to improve cancer imaging and diagnosis.
the development of new imaging technologies that will improve our ability to detect cancer and characterize its metabolic state.
the development of novel methods to image and quantify the metabolic state of cells.
